Ten-pass review: method, findings and claim boundaries
29 September 2026. T en sequential read–challenge–check–rewrite passes over the maintained pDAI
thesis, with a separate model-assisted examination of supply accumulation. This is internal analytical
review, not ten independent reviews, external assurance, a novelty determination or a certificate of
perfection.
Result
The main argument is 1,669 whitespace-delimited words, compared with 3,106 at the start, while
detailed routes, two-sided examples, accumulation accounting and stress conditions are in linked
appendices. The surviving claim is a bounded composition: accepted exclusive claims can access funded
local markets; profitable cycles can transmit demand; and maintained liquidity with retained net outside
income can reinforce later support.
The stronger proposition that controlled validators, unlimited nominal L2 balances and arbitrage alone
imply perfect pDAI stability does not survive. Finite output inventories, two-sided obligations,
incompatible token identities, reference error, delayed funding and controller overshoot give explicit
failure conditions. These do not refute the conditional mechanism. They define the conditions a working
system would have to satisfy.
Review method and questions
Each pass reconsidered the current manuscript, challenged a specific inference, checked its
mathematical or evidence basis, and changed the main text. A machine-readable record retains the
input/output manuscript hashes and word counts for ten distinct revisions; it does not substitute for the
supporting arguments. The sequence is an analytical method, not ten votes for the thesis.
Pass Question tested Finding retained
1 Does control of issuance prove funded
stability?
Authority, accepted claims and output
funding are distinct premises.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 394

Pass Question tested Finding retained
2 Does each route deliver the exact
usable asset and settle?
Eight accounting families require
separate permissions, inventory and
closing obligations.
3 Does relative-price arbitrage define
the dollar target?
A funded anchor or equivalent closing
route is needed; costs and capacity
constrain execution.
4 Does large selling produce a complete
profitable cycle?
The modeled trader profits; treasury
pDAI grows while PLS declines and
eventually exhausts.
5 Does large buying restore the other
side?
The modeled trader profits and
treasury PLS rises; pDAI inventory can
exhaust instead.
6 Does accumulation create favorable
reflexivity?
It can, with maintained depth and
retained net outside income; lending
and LP holdings remain accessible
through their rules.
7 Is stronger coordinated correction
always stabilizing?
Delay and combined response
strength can turn correction into
instability.
8 Which claims are observed on-chain? Saved receipts confirm component
trades and particular mints; the
complete proposed system remains
unverified.
9 Do the bounds withstand adverse
examples and reproduction?
Repeated flows, empty reserves,
reduced depth, losses and reference
error refute the unrestricted claim;
batches reproduce.
10 Can the argument be simpler without
losing its tests?
The main paper states the mechanism
and scope; proofs, examples and full
route diagrams remain traceable in
appendices.
Claim-to-evidence map
Material claim Status and support
A represented receipt can remain invested at source Conditional custody/accounting proposition; historical
bridge models (Appendix 13).
Each named stablecoin already has unrestricted reverse
minting
Not established; exact queried routes and token-specific
capabilities in the issuance inventory (Appendix 4).
Indirect pDAI-supporting arbitrage exists Finite numerical witnesses in the pool-cycle study
(Appendix 47), with an opposite-direction counterexample.
A funded bid and ask supply bounded two-sided conversion Proposed design and arithmetic conditions in the stability
bounds (Appendix 60); not an audited deployed facility.
Large buying after selling can restore support cash Dependent recovery experiment using the prior scenario's
actual ending balances; stability bounds (Appendix 60).
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 395

Material claim Status and support
Accumulation can reduce later sell pressure Conditional comparison at maintained depth; supply
accumulation (Appendix 65). Reduced depth reverses the
example.
More ownership necessarily means more spendable
income
False without activity, attribution and net-cost conditions;
the same accumulation study separates fees, claims, cash
and losses.
Demand inevitably starts at $1 after sellers leave Unverified behavioral hypothesis. Timing, size, persistence
and return of selling require evidence.
Curve, Convex, Frax, Aave and Balancer can be financially
connected
Published architecture and selected local component
evidence; pool-cycle study (Appendix 47), route atlas
(Appendix 51).
Controlling validators makes the system decentralized Does not follow. Operational dependence, entry,
governance and failure of the controlling group require
their own specification.
Current PulseChain records prove a perpetual peg Not established by the evidence audit (Appendix 32).
Numerical and historical verification
The original pool-cycle batch was reproduced byte-for-byte, including its integer conservation checks.
The new stability and dependent recovery batches also reproduced byte-for-byte. They use 70-digit
Decimal arithmetic and relative conservation tolerance 10^-45; they are not EVM execution tests. The two
analytical correction optima were separately checked against neighboring trade sizes and closed surplus
formulas. Supply-depth examples were compared with exact fractions, and local controller stability with
characteristic roots.
The new tests include large selling, large buying, eight-shock one-sided stress, zero-bid and zero-ask
capacity, buying after selling, PLS-reference declines, retained versus withdrawn depth, positive gross
fees with either positive net income or net loss, and delayed corrective responses. Some are
deterministic scenario calculations and others elementary inequalities. They do not sample all market
states, prove global dynamic stability or forecast adoption.
An offline recheck matched 820 saved Curve events to logs in their successful receipts, in 820
distinct transactions. It also rechecked exact input/output transfers in transaction 
0x7f61b4042a71edb340898e3ad46abc01c4d8ddf7197594d077cbfb426c67a5f1, at block 27,264,036: 
13,489.157023144354307302 mUSD into the pool and 564.501482257993107424 DAI to the
examined wallet. The saved reserve summary confirms zero cash and unbacked caps for the three
sampled stablecoin reserves. This is a check of retained records, not a new chain-wide query or
independent node consensus. The older appendices retain their own original audit scope.
The repository research suite completed with 63 tests and 82 subtests passed using ./scripts/test.sh
--research. Those regression tests cover the research codebase; the explicit numerical checks above
validate the new model results. Passing either is not proof that the proposed financial system is
deployed.
Reproduction references
The maintained inputs are:
Research/experiments/pulsechain_pool_cycles_20260929.json, using Research/scripts/
model_pulsechain_pool_cycles.py.
• 
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 396

Research/experiments/pulsechain_stability_review_20260929.json, using Research/scripts/
model_pulsechain_stability.py.
Research/experiments/pulsechain_stability_recovery_20260929.json, using the same stability script and the
preceding final-state dependency.
Fresh output commands and reference locations are in the two numerical studies. The outputs include
script and input hashes. The scoped ignored directory artifacts/pulsechain-stability-review-20260929/
contains results.json, recovery-results.json, adverse-checks.json, historical-evidence-check.json and review-
checkpoints.json. Source snapshots and retrieval hashes are under its sources/ directory. These are working
evidence, not duplicate prose reports.
The anonymous release supplies the concise thesis, consolidated appendices, maintained inputs, scripts
and scoped evidence, with an integrity manifest. Public identifiers and historical hashes retain their
meaning; release hashes identify the supplied sanitized bytes. Prior packages and frozen experiments
remain intact.
What a deployed proof would still require
One must specify the actual controllers and loss-bearing parties; operating source chains; exact token
and contract mappings; valid message paths and finality; source custody and destination liabilities;
funded bids, asks and withdrawals; a reference policy; flow, timing and collateral bounds; and a tested
rule for reinvestment and adverse conditions. Historical execution must then connect those components
in the same actual account.
A mathematical guarantee can quantify a declared model and bounded disturbance set. No finite
collection of examples or repeated AI agreement certifies all possible future economic behavior. The
purpose of this review is to expose those quantifiers and make the positive mechanism testable, not to
replace missing premises with rhetorical certainty.
